<reason>B won by exposing the mandate's asymmetry: it prominently flags only the downsized product while rival unit prices and headline-price rises remain easy to miss, so A's claim that shoppers could still verify £1.11 beats £1.25 was never reconciled with A's own account of tiny, inconsistent rival pricing. B also used A's skimpflation concession effectively. A made a strong deception case, but repeatedly restated rather than resolved the selective-salience and steering problem.</reason>
<best_rebuttal>B's Rebuttal 2 and closing contradiction between A5.3 and A5.4 was decisive: A says rival unit prices are designed to be missed, yet claims shoppers will use the rival's £1.25 unit price to judge the flagged product fairly.</best_rebuttal>
